t.E230.agn: In the EU it was previously authorised for the surface treatment of citrus fruit at up to 70 mg/kg. Directive 2003/114/EC removed this entry from the additive list, stating that biphenyl falls within the definition of a plant protection product and should not remain within the scope of food additive legislation. In its 1966–1967 evaluation, the FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Residues (JMPR) had set an ADI of 0–0.125 mg/kg body weight for diphenyl.
t.E230.body: In rats and rabbits, biphenyl is mainly converted to 4-hydroxybiphenyl, which is excreted in the urine either free or conjugated with sulphate and glucuronic acid.
t.E230.eval: No longer authorised as a food additive in the EU: Directive 2003/114/EC removed its use for the surface treatment of citrus peel from the additive list.
t.E230.found.0: Not authorised as a food additive in the EU since Directive 2003/114/EC (formerly citrus surface treatment)
t.E230.prod: Produced chemically by the high-temperature condensation of benzene or from toluene processing residues.
t.E230.regx.0: Removed from the 95/2/EC additive list (citrus surface treatment, 70 mg/kg) by Directive 2003/114/EC; left to plant protection products legislation. Not included in the EU authorised list under 1129/2011.
t.E230.regx.1: Evaluated as a pesticide residue; ADI 0–0.125 mg/kg body weight.
t.E230.summary: A synthetic antifungal. It was used to prevent mould on citrus peel.
t.E230.what: It was a preservative used to prevent mould on the surface of citrus fruit; it is no longer authorised as a food additive in the EU.
